objective: Wire the own-action fast-path poll trigger (BACKLOG.md #24, analysis/24-event-scheduled-now-playing-poll.md) into backend/src/routes/playback.ts: after each of the pause, resume, skip, and previous route handlers' underlying Spotify call succeeds (i.e. after pausePlayback/resumePlayback/skipToNext/skipToPrevious resolves without throwing, and BEFORE or immediately alongside writing the 200 response -- do not delay/await it before responding), call the triggerImmediateNowPlayingPoll() function exported from backend/src/spotify/nowPlaying.ts (added in the just-completed NP1.1) as fire-and-forget (do not await it in the route handler -- the guest's own HTTP response for their playback action must not wait on an extra Spotify round-trip; the poll runs in the background and its result reaches clients via the existing now-playing SSE event separately). triggerImmediateNowPlayingPoll() already internally catches/logs any poll failure and never leaves a stale timer (see NP1.1's own implementation), so no additional error handling is needed around the call itself beyond making sure a synchronous throw (unlikely, but be defensive) can't crash the route handler.
non_goals: Do not touch nowPlaying.ts itself -- NP1.1 already added and tested triggerImmediateNowPlayingPoll(); this task only calls it from playback.ts.

Do not add a trigger call to POST /volume or POST /jukebox-volume-report -- volume changes don't affect which track is playing or play/pause state, so there's nothing for an immediate poll to usefully refresh there. Only pause, resume, skip, and previous get the trigger.

Do not change any existing response shape, status code, or error-handling behavior of the four routes -- the trigger call is purely additive alongside the existing logic, not a replacement for anything.
Do not touch admin.ts's queue-moderation routes (resyncSpotifyQueue) -- out of scope for this task; queue moderation already re-fetches currently-playing internally as part of its own resync logic.
Do not implement the QUOTA_EXCEEDED-vs-rate-limit distinction or the GET /api/device caching fix from analysis/22 -- both are separate, unrelated tasks.
acceptance_criteria: POST /pause calls triggerImmediateNowPlayingPoll() (fire-and-forget, not awaited) after pausePlayback() succeeds, before or without delaying the 200 response.
POST /resume calls triggerImmediateNowPlayingPoll() the same way after resumePlayback() succeeds.
POST /skip calls triggerImmediateNowPlayingPoll() the same way after skipToNext() succeeds.
POST /previous calls triggerImmediateNowPlayingPoll() the same way after skipToPrevious() succeeds.

None of the four routes' response time is meaningfully delayed by the trigger call -- verify by reading the code (the call must not be awaited before res.status(200).json(...)) rather than only by a timing-based test.
POST /volume and POST /jukebox-volume-report are unchanged -- no trigger call added to either.

Existing error-handling paths (trust-mode 403, device-not-resolved 503, Spotify-call failure 502) are completely unchanged -- the trigger only happens on the existing success path, never instead of or intermixed with error handling.

New/updated tests in playback.test.ts confirm triggerImmediateNowPlayingPoll (mocked) is called exactly once after a successful pause/resume/skip/previous, and is NOT called when the underlying Spotify call fails or when the trust-mode/device-not-resolved checks reject the request first.
cd backend && npx tsc --noEmit and npx vitest run both pass clean.
